text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The World Bank has signed an agreement to give Vietnam a loan of $98.61 million to improve water supplies in Hanoi, Hai Phong, Da Nang and Ha Long.
-- The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development is seeking an investment of $130 million to upgrade post-harvest facilities and boost rice exports in the Mekong Delta.
-- The government has shown its commitment to seeking solutions for overcoming the serious, prolonged consequences of toxic chemicals left from the war.
-- The World Bank will launch a $1.2 million programme to help auditing at the biggest commercial banks in Vietnam.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi will visit China at the invitation of Chinese Party leader and President Ziang Zemin.
-- Vietnam says it will not interfere in Cambodia's internal affairs, but has called for the protection of Vietnamese nationals living in Cambodia.
-- More than 1,780 people in Hanoi joined the Communist Party in the first six months of this year.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's Party Chief Truong Tan Sang has said Vietnam wants to close the past and build a new relationship with the United States based on mutual benefit and understanding.
-- Former Communist Party Chief Nguyen Van Linh has urged the young generation to study and follow the example of their revolutionary predecessors.
